title: Swanson and Hugh Butler Reservoirs Land Conveyances Act
official_summary:
Swanson and Hugh Butler Reservoirs Land Conveyances Act

This act provides for the conveyance of certain federal lands located at the Swanson Reservoir and Hugh Butler Reservoir in Nebraska to Hitchcock County and Frontier County, respectively. The counties must manage the land for substantially the same purposes for which they are being used or for (1) certain public recreation purposes, (2) public access, (3) fish and wildlife habitat, or (4) the preservation of the natural character of the land.

Within three years, the Bureau of Reclamation must enter into negotiations to transfer (1) the Swanson Permitted Cabin Land, the Swanson Permitted Concession Land, and the Lakeview Lodge Permitted Concession Land to Hitchcock County; and (2) the Red Willow Permitted Cabin Land and the Red Willow Permitted Concession Land to Frontier County. Reclamation must offer to convey the land as soon as practicable after the title transfer agreement is made. The land must be conveyed in whole and not subdivided. Additionally, the act subjects the conveyances to certain existing rights and requirements. Further, the act limits future conveyances of the land.

Reclamation must enter into a memorandum of agreement with each county to establish and define the roles and responsibilities for actions required to convey the land.

The counties must provide compensation to the Reclamation Fund in an amount equal to the fair market value of the land. The counties must also pay the conveyance costs in advance of the conveyance.

summary.headline: Law transfers certain federal land at two Nebraska reservoirs to Hitchcock County and Frontier County.
summary.what_it_does: The Bureau of Reclamation must negotiate, within three years, to transfer cabin and business (concession) land at Swanson Reservoir to Hitchcock County and at Hugh Butler Reservoir (Red Willow) to Frontier County. The counties must pay fair market value for the land and cover the transfer costs up front. The land must be transferred as a whole, not split up, and the counties must keep using it for its current purposes or for recreation, public access, wildlife habitat, or keeping its natural character. Existing rights stay in place, and future sales of the land are limited.

who_it_affects.group: Hitchcock County and Frontier County, Nebraska
who_it_affects.how: Each county can take ownership of the reservoir land but must pay fair market value and transfer costs and manage it for set uses.

who_it_affects.group: People with permitted cabins or businesses at Swanson and Hugh Butler reservoirs
who_it_affects.how: The land under their cabins or businesses, including Lakeview Lodge, would move from federal to county ownership, with existing rights still honored.
The agency must negotiate with each county, sign agreements on roles, and offer the land for transfer as soon as practical.
The land must stay available for uses like recreation, public access, and wildlife habitat under county management.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 23, 2024; Reclamation must begin transfer negotiations within three years.
